Prévenir l’itinérance après l’avoir vécu: Preventing Homelessness After Having Lived It
À la Coalition Jeunes+, des jeunes ayant: At Coalition Jeunes+, young people who have experienced homelessness are turning their experience into concrete solutions to prevent precarity.
À la suite de notre article « Élections: Following our article “Municipal Elections – Proposals From People Experiencing Homelessness,” we wanted to give a voice to young people who have experienced homelessness, since those under 25 are particularly affected by this crisis and their voices are almost absent from public debate.
C’est dans ce contexte que nous avons dé: It was in this context that we discovered the mission of Coalition Jeunes+, created by the organization Dans la rue, which helps young people experiencing homelessness. The coalition, which aims to develop recommendations to prevent homelessness, is unique in that it includes young people with experience of homelessness in its thinking process.
Nous avons ainsi rencontré Mélodie Corde: We met Mélodie Cordeau, a project manager, and Zachary, a young participant, to discuss their mission at the Coalition – and how they use their lived experience to help prevent homelessness.
<strong>À la Coalition Jeunes+, des jeun: At Coalition Jeunes+, young people are using their experience of homelessness to propose ways to prevent it. A conversation with Mélodie and Zachary.
Sur la rue Ontario Est, les ressources e: On Ontario Street East, homelessness services follow one another closely. I was asked to meet outside the Dans la rue day centre. The building is easy to recognize, with a truck in the organization’s colours parked out front; the organization helps young people experiencing homelessness. Seeing me arrive, Mélodie Cordeau greets me with a big smile. The light-eyed woman in her thirties is <l1>project manager at Coalition Jeunes+</l1>, whose mission is to prevent homelessness among young people, while its parent organization, Dans la rue, responds to it.
Nous montons à l’étage et nous nous inst: We go upstairs and settle into a small room tucked away in a maze of hallways. Mélodie seems to know the place well; she has worked at the Coalition for six years – and “almost 10 years in the community sector” in homelessness, she says with a touch of pride.
Avant cela, elle a elle-même été en situ: Before that, she herself experienced homelessness. “I’m a young person with experiential knowledge of homelessness,” she explains. It was that experience of the street that led her to get involved.
Mélodie a été en situation d’itinérance: Mélodie experienced homelessness from age 16 to 22, after losing her housing following the death of her partner. She also had mental health and drug use problems, which she says contributed to isolating her even more.
Elle a passé l’essentiel de cette périod: She spent most of that period in downtown Montréal, building a “micro-community” with other young people experiencing homelessness. She is “one of the only ones” to have survived, she says. “That’s why I chose to get involved in the community sector. I wanted to give back to the community and make the most of the fact that I was still here,” she continues.
Quelques semaines après être sortie de l: A few weeks after leaving homelessness, she began volunteering as a peer support worker, before landing various positions in the field. She then realized she could “directly use [her] lived experience to help others,” says the woman who is now a project manager in homelessness prevention.
<strong>Par et pour les jeunes en situat: By and for young people experiencing homelessness
Au sein de la Coalition Jeunes+, Mélodie: At Coalition Jeunes+, Mélodie oversees a committee of about ten young people tasked with developing recommendations to prevent youth homelessness. Among them is Zachary, 22, who joined the Coalition “about eight months ago.” With long hair and a cap on his head, Zachary finds his way around the organization’s hallways as easily as Mélodie does. Originally from the South Shore, Zachary is Two-Spirit and alternates between the pronouns he and she.
Comme les autres membres du comité, Zach: Like the other committee members, Zachary has direct experience of homelessness. Diagnosed with bipolar I disorder, he had a psychotic episode in the summer of 2023, which led to homelessness after a stay in a psychiatric hospital. “It’s an illness that, if left untreated, can have uncontrollable repercussions on your life,” he says. What followed was a “long six-month period of uncertainty, precarity and major struggles.”
C’est à la Maison Tangente, où il occupa: It was at Maison Tangente, where he had a transitional apartment, that he heard about Coalition Jeunes+. After a few conversations and brainstorming activities on several issues, he decided to get involved for the long term. “I thought: ‘Well, why not? I’ll give it a try!’” he says. “Because I was given so much by community resources that it’s extremely important to me to try to give that back,” he adds.
Si la Coalition fait appel à des personn: The Coalition calls on people with close experience of homelessness in order to propose recommendations “aligned with the reality of young people and what they truly need,” explains Mélodie. “The six years I spent on the street are worth as much as a research project that lasted six years,” says the project manager.
Zachary estime également que « les gens: Zachary likewise believes that “people who have lived through homelessness, mental health issues and precarity are the real experts on these questions.”
La Coalition s’appuie ainsi sur les reco: The Coalition thus draws on recommendations from young people, but also from researchers and organizations, to propose possible solutions to prevent youth homelessness. According to Mélodie, this means “understanding what could have been done earlier in young people’s lives so that this situation would have been avoided.”
Au-delà des ressources d’urgence, la pré: Beyond emergency services, the Coalition believes prevention is essential to tackling a homelessness crisis in which young people are among the main victims. In Canada, one in two people experiencing homelessness is under 25 or had their first episode of homelessness before that age, according to Statistics Canada.
« Ça n’a pas de sens de toujours essayer: “It makes no sense to keep trying to put out the fire without asking what started it, and how we could have prevented it,” Mélodie says. In her view, we need to move from a “palliative perspective to a preventive perspective” by launching structural changes.
La Ville de Montréal a annoncé au début: In early January, the City of Montréal announced its 2026 budget – in which it plans to triple the amount allocated to fighting homelessness.
De 9,8 M$ l’année dernière, l’enveloppe: From $9.8 million last year, the envelope rises to nearly $30 million, which will be invested to support community organizations working with people experiencing homelessness or in social cohabitation.
« En une seule année, notre administrati: “In a single year, our administration is putting in more than everything the previous administration put in over four years. It’s unprecedented for the City when it comes to homelessness,” Claude Pinard, chair of the executive committee, said at a press conference during the presentation of the City’s budget.
L’administration Ferrada Martinez compte: The Ferrada Martinez administration also plans to spend $578 million by 2035 to acquire new buildings in order to improve the supply of affordable and social housing.
« Nous allons tout faire pour offrir à c: “We will do everything we can to offer every Montrealer dignified and safe conditions,” Claude Pinard said in January.
Au-delà des sommes allouées à l’itinéran: Beyond the sums allocated to homelessness overall, Mélodie and Zachary are calling on public authorities for measures tailored to young people, to be put in place well before they end up without a fixed address.
Les jeunes de la Coalition appellent ain: The young people of the Coalition are therefore calling for improvements to young people’s living conditions upstream. The housing, education and access to information currently available to young people do not protect them enough from precarity and homelessness, they say, and they lacked this in their own journeys.
S’il y a une cause commune à l’itinéranc: If there is one common cause of youth homelessness, Mélodie says, it is a lack of resources. “By definition, when you’re young, you generally have a lower income, less of a network, less information and fewer skills,” Mélodie explains. While adults experiencing homelessness lose their autonomy, young people haven’t had time to gain it.
La première ressource qui leur manque es: The first resource they lack is financial. For Zachary, there are “really simple things we can do to prevent youth homelessness,” starting with improving access to housing. Mélodie believes she might have made different choices if she had had the means to afford housing. “A decent income is also the foundation,” she says, noting that she received no social assistance for most of her time experiencing homelessness.
L’autre ressource dont elle aurait aimé: The other resource she wishes she had had more of is education. Not the kind that deals with math or French – which “schools focus on” – but “life skills” that allow young people to gain autonomy and self-knowledge. “No one makes sure young people have the tools to become adults,” Mélodie laments, when this new life is “full of moments of turmoil” that can lead to homelessness.
La jeune femme milite aussi pour que les: The young woman also advocates for educational settings to listen more and create more safe spaces, relying for example on peer support. “Because it’s hard to open up to adults about what you’re going through,” she says. As a teenager, she would have liked a “safe space where, even if [she] had opened up about her drug use, [she] wouldn’t have been reprimanded.” She believes that could have “influenced the choices made afterward.”
Enfin, nombreux sont ceux qui estiment q: Finally, many believe young people lack information about available support resources. Whether during an episode of homelessness or for any other issue. “You don’t know where to go, you don’t know what to do,” Mélodie recalls. “It would have helped me a lot to learn at school that youth centres existed.”
Alors qu’il vivait une situation d’itiné: While he was experiencing homelessness and a crisis linked to his bipolar disorder, Zachary deliberately committed an offence in order to be incarcerated and thus “have access to services,” he says. “I had no idea that places like shelters existed, and I wasn’t able to take in information,” he says regretfully.
Certains jeunes sont surreprésentés dans: Some young people are overrepresented among those experiencing homelessness, such as those who have been through youth protection (DPJ), a third of whom experience homelessness before age 21. Young people from the 2SLGBTQIA+ community make up 40% of users of the organization Dans la rue. Communities more exposed to precarity, such as racialized or Indigenous people, are at greater risk of youth homelessness, Mélodie notes.
Toutefois, « il n’y a pas une cause uniq: However, “there isn’t a single cause of homelessness,” believes the project manager. It is important, she says, not to forget that some people in “tough situations” do very well, and that others, who are better off, fall into precarity.
Pour la Coalition, il est essentiel que: For the Coalition, it is essential that all young people have access to economic and social resources. Because “any young person can end up in a situation where you simply can’t afford rent, you don’t have the tools, you don’t have the references, you don’t have the money,” Mélodie says.
C’est « l’ensemble de la structure » qu’: It is “the entire structure” that needs to be rethought if we want to effectively prevent precarity and homelessness among young people, Mélodie believes. Quebec, she adds, has the means and resources needed to make the necessary changes. “We’re able to invest massively in military defence, businesses, hockey teams, but we can’t invest, even minimally, for the good of a community?” she asks.
Zachary a l’impression qu’en dehors de N: Zachary feels that outside of Christmas, when “everyone does the media rounds,” society tends to “sweep the subject under the rug.” Yet it is an issue that affects everyone, he says, since “most of us are closer to being on the street than to being millionaires.”
Au-delà de la prévention de l’itinérance: Beyond preventing homelessness, the practices encouraged by Zachary, Mélodie and the Coalition’s young people “also help young people become autonomous, healthy, responsible and engaged adults.” And quite simply “promote young people’s rights, which at the moment are not being respected,” Mélodie concludes.
Au moment de publier ces lignes, la Vill: At the time of publication, the City had not responded to our interview request.
Voici les pistes de solutions pour lutte: Here are the possible solutions for fighting youth homelessness, according to the young people we spoke with:
Écouter les jeunes ayant vécu en situati: Listen to young people who have experienced homelessness and include them in decision-making.
Agir en amont de l’itinérance, pour la p: Act upstream of homelessness to prevent it in a lasting way.
Améliorer les conditions de vie des jeun: Improve young people’s living conditions: access to housing, the fight against precarity, a decent income for all.
Faciliter l’accès des jeunes à l’informa: Make it easier for young people to access information about support resources.
Une éducation plus adaptée aux problémat: Education better suited to the challenges encountered in the transition to adulthood.
Dans les milieux éducatifs, offrir aux j: In educational settings, offer young people more listening and safe spaces.
Dans les ressources d’aide, favoriser l’: In support services, favour the “by and for” approach.
